comments.why: Pumped storage as lake-based electricity generation.
comments.text: I'd say it's a quite big one, "every city" has water towers to provide pressure to the people living in it, or they rely on the water source if it's higher up than the city. There are probably exceptions, where this isn't true, but raised tanks make modern society possible. [LINK] more on water towers, which are raised tanks of water. We also pump water into fake lakes to later extract electricity from it. ( [VIDEO] ) Another good thing with water towers is that we can keep running the pumps at a lower RPM where efficiency than if we were trying to build a system with pumps to keep pressure. Great channel if you're curious about everything related to humans relationship with water.

comments.text: Looks like the high-voltage transmission lines are very efficient, losing only a few percent over hundreds of miles: [LINK] There's a good watch on pumped hydro, and how it is kinda sucky: [VIDEO] Battery storage is the most likely thing, although there is also kinetic storage (flywheels) and some other ideas as well (ultracapacitors, for instance).

comments.story: Ditch the Batteries: Off-Grid Compressed Air Energy Storage (2018)
comments.why: Demo showing small energy in elevated water.
comments.text: You could start by just calculating the potential energy of the volume of the tank you are considering, and the difference in elevation between the reservoirs (volume x 1 kg/L x gravity x elevation difference, plug in the units of your choice and let google figure it out). I suspect the amount of energy is far less than you are imagining... It takes a lot of water to generate a useful amount of energy. This video ( [VIDEO] ) does an interesting demo and points out that a 5 gallon bucket on a ladder has the same potential energy as a watch battery.
